title: DNF and CNF forms of shallow restricted gates
statement: Let $g_1,\dots,g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, let $\rho$ be a restriction of these variables, and let $l\in\bbn$. For each $i$, write $f_i$ for the restriction of $g_i$ by $\rho$, that is, the Boolean function $x \mapsto g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ that evaluates $g_i$ with the coordinates fixed by $\rho$ set accordingly and the free coordinates supplied by $x$, and suppose that every $f_i$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then for each $i$ there is a DNF formula $\varphi_i$ of width at most $l$ that computes $f_i$, in which no term repeats a literal and no two literals of the same term share a variable; and there is a CNF formula $\psi_i$ of width at most $l$ that also computes $f_i$.
hypotheses_covered: m gates, each a DNF formula on n variables
a restriction ρ of the n variables
for every gate i, the restriction of g_i by ρ has decision-tree depth at most l
replaced:
If, after applying a restriction $\rho$, every gate function
$\mathrm{restrictFn}\,(\mathrm{gates}\,i).\mathrm{eval}\,\rho$ has decision-tree depth at
most $l$, then each gate admits both a width-$l$ DNF representation (whose terms are
duplicate-free and contain no two literals on the same variable) and a width-$l$ CNF
representation, each computing the same function.
